title: Harvard Physical Sciences 2 randomized trial: LLM-based AI tutor (GPT-4) doubles learning gains versus in-class active learning
summary: Harvard PS2 RCT (fall 2023, 194 students): LLM-based tutor (GPT-4) produced over double the learning gains of active-learning class in less time.
account: In autumn 2023 the course team of Harvard University's Physical Sciences 2 ran a randomized controlled crossover experiment with 194 students. It covered two topics, surface tension and fluid flow. Each student learned one topic in an in-class active-learning session and the other at home with a purpose-built AI tutor. The paper does not state outright which model the tutor ran on. Its Methods say “we avoided relying solely on GPT-4 to generate solutions for these activities”. Its Discussion lists “a large language model capable of closely following complex prompts (e.g., GPT-4)” among the factors behind the gains. The paper was published in Scientific Reports on 3 June 2025. It reports that “students learn significantly more in less time when using the AI tutor”. Median learning gains were over double those of the class session, with a median of 49 minutes on task, and higher engagement and motivation. The paper places the study in “the Fall 2023 semester” and “the ninth and tenth weeks of the course” without a calendar date. The lessons themselves came later in the term.
purpose: The tutor was built to teach these physics lessons with research-based pedagogy. The learning gain was that purpose.
system: Custom AI tutor for Harvard PS2 built on a large language model with research-based pedagogical prompts
developer: Harvard University (Kestin, Miller, Klales, Milbourne, Ponti)

ratings.reason: A randomized trial reporting class-level learning gains. Students in the AI condition scored higher on a post-test for one lesson (median gains over double) in a median of 49 minutes. A small, short-term benefit per student.
A randomized trial reporting class-level learning gains. The course gained evidence for a lesson format that teaches a topic in less time with higher reported engagement.

ai_role.statement: The language model delivered the instruction. The comparison was active learning taught in class. The authors credit the research-based design (prompts, scaffolding) beside the model.

evidence.citation: Kestin G, Miller K, Klales A, Milbourne T, Ponti G (2025). AI tutoring outperforms in-class active learning: an RCT introducing a novel research-based design in an authentic educational setting. Scientific Reports (PMC12179260).

evidence.quote: students learn significantly more in less time when using the AI tutor, compared with the in-class active learning

produced_by: Lesson content pre-structured by instructors into the tutor

must_hold: The model follows complex pedagogical prompts

echoes.setting: Edo State, Nigeria: six-week after-school program (June-July 2024; first day of month used) for first-year senior secondary students in Benin City using Microsoft Copilot (GPT-4); 0.31 SD overall, 0.23 SD in English; World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11125 (May 2025)
echoes.source: ERIC record ED676624 https://eric.ed.gov/?q=source:%22World+Bank%22&id=ED676624 (quote: 'a significant improvement of 0.31 standard deviation'); World Bank blog 9 Jan 2025 https://blogs.worldbank.org/en/education/From-chalkboards-to-chatbots-Transforming-learning-in-Nigeria (quote: 'equivalent to nearly two years of typical learning in just six weeks')
